content.thinking: The deploy timestamp lines up exactly with the latency spike—p50 jumping from 44 to 186, p95 from 220 to 905, p99 from 380 to 1519—while error rate stayed low, confirming this is a bad deployment causing the "HighLatency" alert rather than an error-driven issue. The ClientDisconnected errors in the logs likely stem from shoppers giving up on slow responses.

hypotheses.subject: 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655
hypotheses.summary: A deployment at 13:26:00Z (revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655) landed exactly at the onset of the latency spike: p50 jumped from ~44ms to 186-460ms, p95 from ~220ms to 2100-2240ms, and p99 from ~380ms to 3750-3870ms within the same minute the deploy occurred, with no corresponding change in request volume or memory. The logs show a rising trail of ClientDisconnected errors (shoppers timing out) immediately following, consistent with new code performing much slower per request.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection

hypotheses.subject: 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655
hypotheses.summary: If the deploy only altered configuration (e.g. a timeout, connection pool size, or backend endpoint) rather than code, the same latency jump could be explained by a broken config value pointing at a healthy but now misconfigured dependency; the evidence available does not distinguish a code change from a config change within the deploy.

supporting_evidence.claim: p50/p95/p99 latency all jumped 4-10x in the same minute as the deploy with flat request_volume and memory

hypotheses.summary: No further cause identified beyond the deploy correlation; memory, request volume and error rate stayed essentially flat, so resource exhaustion or an upstream dependency failure are not supported by the data collected.
